name: MetaAdsMCP
title: Instagram Ads
description: Run Instagram ad campaigns. Find targeting, create campaigns and image ads paused, pause them, read their results.
whenToUse: Pick to advertise on Instagram: find an ad account, the Instagram account to post as and the targeting to use (countries, job titles, industries, interests), create a campaign and its image ads, pause it or lower its budget, and read spend and results per campaign. Campaigns are created paused and this node never switches one on, so nothing it does spends more. Attach it via a service edge to an agent, or trigger it directly to list the accounts.

inputs.name: input
inputs.description: Trigger. When the graph runs this node it lists the ad accounts and Instagram accounts the token can reach.

outputs.name: output
outputs.description: The ad accounts and Instagram accounts, or Meta's reason it could not list them

authRequired.title: Require sign-in
authRequired.description: Only a signed-in caller may run this step. Leave off and it runs for whoever the workflow's trigger admitted, which is the usual answer.

authRole.title: Require role
authRole.description: A claim the caller's account must carry, as noun:verb (finance:approve, payments:refund). Leave blank to require only that they are signed in.

package.name: meta
package.packageFile:
# FULLY DECLARATIVE. package.yaml, nodes/, credentials/ and shared/, nothing else.
#
# Meta's Graph API, for Instagram: ad accounts, targeting, campaigns, image ads and their
# results (the Marketing API), and posts on our own Instagram account (Content Publishing).
# Every endpoint is from Meta's own docs at developers.facebook.com, Graph API v26.0.
#
# Every write is a multipart form, because that is how Meta's docs send every Marketing API
# call; a nested parameter (targeting, a creative's story) is JSON in its own field, which is
# how the form encoding already carries an object.

name: meta
displayName: Meta
description: Instagram ads and posts for Unoverse
version: 1.0.0
category: communication

features:
  - Find ad accounts, the Instagram account to post as, and targeting (countries, job titles, industries, interests)
  - Create Instagram campaigns, created paused, and image ads
  - Pause a campaign or lower its budget; switching on is a separate node, for a task that asks a person first
  - Read spend and results per campaign
  - Publish an image post on our Instagram account, as a separate node, for a task that asks a person first

# Meta fetches every image itself, from the url it is given, so no call here fetches one.
allowedHosts:
  - graph.facebook.com

requires:
  credential: [bearer]
  transport: [json]
  # A post's image is processed before it may be published, so the post node waits on it.
  poll: true
  executorVersion: ">=1.2.0"

credentials.metaAccessToken.yaml:
# The SHAPE only; values live encrypted in Postgres on a deployed universe.

name: metaAccessToken
displayName: Meta
description: >-
  A system user's access token from our Meta Business account. A system user acts for the
  business rather than a person, so this works with nobody signed in.
documentationUrl: https://developers.facebook.com/docs/marketing-api/system-users/install-apps-and-generate-tokens/

properties:
  - name: token
    displayName: Access Token
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: >-
      Made in Business Settings, System users, Generate token, for our app, with the ad account,
      the Facebook Page and the Instagram account assigned to the system user, and the
      permissions ads_management, ads_read, pages_show_list, pages_read_engagement,
      instagram_basic and instagram_content_publish. A 60-day token must be made again before
      it runs out.

shared.api.yaml:
# What every Meta call shares. The API version is in each url (graph.facebook.com/v26.0);
# Meta keeps a version for two years after the next ships, so bump them together.

credential: &credential
  scheme: bearer
  token: "{{ credentials.metaAccessToken.token }}"

# Meta answers a failure with a 400 and an `error`, carrying the reason a person can read in
# `error_user_msg` when there is one. Each call takes the 400 as an answer (`okOn`) so that
# reason reaches the caller here, rather than the transport's raw status line.
error: &error
  when: "return !!(response && response.error)"
  message: "return response.error.error_user_msg || response.error.message || 'Meta rejected the request'"
shared.schema.yaml:
# TOOL DISCOVERY, as DATA: what an attached Agent reads before it reaches Meta. The wording
# IS the routing: a model reads these descriptions when choosing a tool, so rephrasing is a
# behaviour change, never a tidy-up. The argument shapes are what the model fills in.

meta:
  name: Instagram Ads
  version: "1.0.0"
  description: >-
    Run Instagram ad campaigns: find ad accounts, the Instagram account and targeting, create
    campaigns and image ads paused, pause them or lower their budget, and read spend and
    results.
  instructions: |-
    INSTAGRAM ADS PROTOCOL:
    - Start with list_accounts. Every other tool takes an ad account's id; create_ad takes a Page's page_id and instagram_account_id.
    - Targeting values are ids (two-letter codes for countries). Find them with find_targeting before create_campaign; never guess one.
    - create_campaign makes a PAUSED campaign, which spends nothing. Switching a campaign on, or raising its budget, is a person's yes and is never done here.
    - Job titles, industries and interests together are one OR group, inside the countries given.
    - Never aim at anyone by gender, age, race or ethnicity.
    - A tool that fails carries Meta's reason. Say so rather than claiming it worked.
  methods:
    list_accounts:
      description: >-
        List the ad accounts you can manage, with id and currency, and the Facebook Pages with
        the Instagram account each posts as.
      input:
        type: object
        properties: {}

    find_targeting:
      description: >-
        Find the targeting ids for one kind: countries, job_titles, industries or interests, by
        search text, or with no text every industry.
      input:
        type: object
        properties:
          kind:
            type: string
            enum: [countries, job_titles, industries, interests]
            description: The kind of targeting.
          query:
            type: string
            description: >-
              Search text, e.g. "United Arab Emirates", "Head of Customer Experience",
              "banking". Needed for countries, job titles and interests.
        required: [kind]

    list_campaigns:
      description: >-
        List an ad account's campaigns that are on or paused, with status, daily budget and
        objective.
      input:
        type: object
        properties:
          account_id:
            type: string
            description: The ad account's id, from list_accounts.
        required: [account_id]

    create_campaign:
      description: >-
        Create an Instagram campaign, PAUSED so it spends nothing until a person switches it
        on. Give it a name, a daily budget in the account's currency, an objective and its
        targeting.
      input:
        type: object
        properties:
          account_id:
            type: string
            description: The ad account's id.
          name:
            type: string
            description: What the campaign is for, e.g. "Gulf bank CX leaders, October".
          daily_budget:
            type: number
            description: Most to spend per day, in the account's currency.
          objective:
            type: string
            enum: [TRAFFIC, AWARENESS]
            description: TRAFFIC (clicks to a page, the default) or AWARENESS (to be seen).
          countries:
            type: array
            items: { type: string }
            description: Two-letter country codes from find_targeting, e.g. ["AE", "SA"].
          job_titles:
            type: array
            items: { type: string }
            description: Job title ids from find_targeting (optional).
          industries:
            type: array
            items: { type: string }
            description: Industry ids from find_targeting (optional).
          interests:
            type: array
            items: { type: string }
            description: Interest ids from find_targeting (optional).
        required: [account_id, name, daily_budget, countries]

    create_ad:
      description: >-
        Create an image ad in a campaign's ad set, posted as our Instagram account: the words,
        an image by its https url, a headline, and the page it links to.
      input:
        type: object
        properties:
          account_id:
            type: string
            description: The ad account's id.
          ad_set_id:
            type: string
            description: The campaign's ad set id, from create_campaign.
          page_id:
            type: string
            description: The Facebook Page's id, from list_accounts.
          instagram_account_id:
            type: string
            description: That Page's Instagram account id, from list_accounts.
          text:
            type: string
            description: The caption under the image. The first 125 characters show before "more".
          image_url:
            type: string
            description: An https url of a JPG or PNG, square (1080 by 1080) or portrait (1080 by 1350).
          headline:
            type: string
            description: The headline, short.
          landing_page:
            type: string
            description: The https page the ad links to.
          call_to_action:
            type: string
            enum: [LEARN_MORE, SIGN_UP, DOWNLOAD, SUBSCRIBE, APPLY_NOW, CONTACT_US]
            description: The button's label (optional, LEARN_MORE when left out).
        required: [account_id, ad_set_id, page_id, instagram_account_id, text, image_url, headline, landing_page]

    change_campaign:
      description: >-
        Pause or archive a campaign, or lower its daily budget. It never switches a campaign on
        or raises a budget: those spend more, and are a person's yes.
      input:
        type: object
        properties:
          campaign_id:
            type: string
            description: The campaign's id.
          status:
            type: string
            enum: [PAUSED, ARCHIVED]
            description: Pause it, or archive it (optional).
          daily_budget:
            type: number
            description: A lower daily budget (optional), in the account's currency.
        required: [campaign_id]

    report:
      description: >-
        Spend and results per campaign in an ad account, from a start date (YYYY-MM-DD, default
        30 days ago) to today or an end date. Optionally only some campaigns.
      input:
        type: object
        properties:
          account_id:
            type: string
            description: The ad account's id.
          since:
            type: string
            description: Start date, YYYY-MM-DD (optional, default 30 days ago).
          until:
            type: string
            description: End date, YYYY-MM-DD (optional, default today).
          campaign_ids:
            type: array
            items: { type: string }
            description: Only these campaigns (optional).
        required: [account_id]
shared.shape.yaml:
# The ad accounts and the Instagram accounts to post as, bounded to what a caller decides with:
# an account's id for every other tool, its currency for a budget, and each Page's Instagram
# account, which every ad and post is posted as.
#
# Here once, because the graph run (events.yaml) and the list_accounts tool answer with the
# same shape.
accounts: &accounts >-
  return {
    ok: true,
    ad_accounts: ((calls.adaccounts || {}).data || []).map(a => ({
      id: String(a.account_id),
      name: a.name,
      currency: a.currency,
      active: a.account_status === 1
    })),
    pages: ((calls.pages || {}).data || []).map(p => ({
      page_id: String(p.id),
      name: p.name,
      instagram_account_id: p.instagram_business_account ? String(p.instagram_business_account.id) : null
    }))
  }

files.api/events.yaml:
# One row, one connector: the accounts, in the same shape list_accounts answers with.

- emit: output
  from: response
  value: { $ref: shape#accounts }
files.api/run.yaml:
# Triggered by the graph, this node lists the ad accounts and the Instagram accounts the token
# can reach: the read that proves the token works, and the ids every tool needs.

- name: adaccounts
  method: GET
  url: "https://graph.facebook.com/v26.0/me/adaccounts?fields=account_id,name,currency,account_status"
  credential: { $ref: api#credential }
  transport: json
  okOn: [400, 403]
  error: { $ref: api#error }

- name: pages
  method: GET
  url: "https://graph.facebook.com/v26.0/me/accounts?fields=id,name,instagram_business_account"
  credential: { $ref: api#credential }
  transport: json
  okOn: [400, 403]
  error: { $ref: api#error }
files.api/service.yaml:
# The MCP methods an agent can call, over Meta's Marketing API: what an agent running Instagram
# ads does, and nothing that creates accounts, manages their users, deletes, or spends more.
#
# A CAMPAIGN HOLDS THE BUDGET AND THE SWITCH. Its daily budget is the campaign's own (Meta's
# campaign budget), and it is created paused; its one ad set and its ads are created on, so
# nothing serves until the campaign is, and switching on is one change in one place.
#
# BUDGETS ARE IN THE CURRENCY'S SMALLEST UNIT on the wire (cents for USD, fils for AED), so
# a budget in the account's currency is multiplied by 100 going out and divided coming back.
# Meta gives a few currencies (JPY, KRW and others) an offset of 1; none is ours.

getSchema:
  description: Tool discovery for Instagram ads
  calls: []
  returns: { $ref: schema#meta }

list_accounts:
  description: >-
    List the ad accounts you can manage, with id and currency, and the Facebook Pages with the
    Instagram account each posts as.
  calls:
    - name: adaccounts
      method: GET
      url: "https://graph.facebook.com/v26.0/me/adaccounts?fields=account_id,name,currency,account_status"
      credential: { $ref: api#credential }
      transport: json
      okOn: [400, 403]
      error: { $ref: api#error }
    - name: pages
      method: GET
      url: "https://graph.facebook.com/v26.0/me/accounts?fields=id,name,instagram_business_account"
      credential: { $ref: api#credential }
      transport: json
      okOn: [400, 403]
      error: { $ref: api#error }
  returns: { $ref: shape#accounts }

find_targeting:
  description: >-
    Find the targeting ids for one kind: countries, job_titles, industries or interests, by
    search text, or with no text every industry.
  calls:
    - name: search
      method: GET
      url: >-
        return 'https://graph.facebook.com/v26.0/search?limit=50&'
          + (params.kind === 'countries' ? 'type=adgeolocation&location_types=' + encodeURIComponent('["country"]') + '&q=' + encodeURIComponent(params.query || '')
            : params.kind === 'job_titles' ? 'type=adworkposition&q=' + encodeURIComponent(params.query || '')
            : params.kind === 'industries' ? 'type=adTargetingCategory&class=industries'
            : 'type=adinterest&q=' + encodeURIComponent(params.query || ''))
      credential: { $ref: api#credential }
      transport: json
      okOn: [400, 403]
      error: { $ref: api#error }
  # A country is targeted by its two-letter code, everything else by its id.
  returns: >-
    return {
      ok: true,
      kind: params.kind,
      values: (response.data || [])
        .filter(v => params.kind !== 'industries' || !params.query || String(v.name).toLowerCase().indexOf(String(params.query).toLowerCase()) !== -1)
        .slice(0, 50)
        .map(v => ({ id: params.kind === 'countries' ? v.key : String(v.id), name: v.name }))
    }

list_campaigns:
  description: >-
    List an ad account's campaigns that are on or paused, with status, daily budget and
    objective.
  calls:
    - name: campaigns
      method: GET
      url: >-
        return 'https://graph.facebook.com/v26.0/act_' + encodeURIComponent(params.account_id)
          + '/campaigns?fields=id,name,status,effective_status,objective,daily_budget&limit=50'
          + '&effective_status=' + encodeURIComponent('["ACTIVE","PAUSED","IN_PROCESS","WITH_ISSUES"]')
      credential: { $ref: api#credential }
      transport: json
      okOn: [400, 403]
      error: { $ref: api#error }
  returns: >-
    return {
      ok: true,
      campaigns: (response.data || []).map(c => ({
        id: String(c.id),
        name: c.name,
        status: c.status,
        serving: c.effective_status,
        objective: c.objective,
        daily_budget: c.daily_budget ? Number(c.daily_budget) / 100 : null
      })),
      has_more: !!((response.paging || {}).next)
    }

create_campaign:
  description: >-
    Create an Instagram campaign, PAUSED so it spends nothing until a person switches it on.
    Give it a name, a daily budget in the account's currency, an objective and its targeting.
  calls:
    - name: campaign
      method: POST
      url: "return 'https://graph.facebook.com/v26.0/act_' + encodeURIComponent(params.account_id) + '/campaigns'"
      credential: { $ref: api#credential }
      encoding: multipart
      body: >-
        return {
          name: String(params.name),
          objective: params.objective === 'AWARENESS' ? 'OUTCOME_AWARENESS' : 'OUTCOME_TRAFFIC',
          status: 'PAUSED',
          special_ad_categories: [],
          daily_budget: Math.round(Number(params.daily_budget) * 100),
          bid_strategy: 'LOWEST_COST_WITHOUT_CAP'
        }
      transport: json
      okOn: [400, 403]
      error: { $ref: api#error }
    # Instagram's feed, stories and reels only. Explore is refused by v26. Advantage+ audience
    # is off, so the targeting given is the targeting used; job titles, industries and
    # interests are one OR group, as Meta's flexible_spec reads them.
    - name: adset
      method: POST
      url: "return 'https://graph.facebook.com/v26.0/act_' + encodeURIComponent(params.account_id) + '/adsets'"
      credential: { $ref: api#credential }
      encoding: multipart
      body: >-
        return {
          name: String(params.name),
          campaign_id: String(calls.campaign.id),
          billing_event: 'IMPRESSIONS',
          optimization_goal: params.objective === 'AWARENESS' ? 'REACH' : 'LINK_CLICKS',
          status: 'ACTIVE',
          targeting: Object.fromEntries(Object.entries({
            geo_locations: { countries: params.countries },
            publisher_platforms: ['instagram'],
            instagram_positions: ['stream', 'story', 'reels'],
            targeting_automation: { advantage_audience: 0 },
            flexible_spec: [Object.fromEntries(Object.entries({
              work_positions: (params.job_titles || []).map(id => ({ id: String(id) })),
              industries: (params.industries || []).map(id => ({ id: String(id) })),
              interests: (params.interests || []).map(id => ({ id: String(id) }))
            }).filter(e => e[1].length > 0))].filter(f => Object.keys(f).length > 0)
          }).filter(e => !Array.isArray(e[1]) || e[1].length > 0))
        }
      transport: json
      okOn: [400, 403]
      error: { $ref: api#error }
  returns: >-
    return { ok: true, campaign_id: String(calls.campaign.id), ad_set_id: String(calls.adset.id), status: 'PAUSED' }

create_ad:
  description: >-
    Create an image ad in a campaign's ad set, posted as our Instagram account: the words, an
    image by its https url, a headline, and the page it links to.
  calls:
    # Meta fetches the image from its url itself (link_data.picture), so nothing is uploaded.
    - name: creative
      method: POST
      url: "return 'https://graph.facebook.com/v26.0/act_' + encodeURIComponent(params.account_id) + '/adcreatives'"
      credential: { $ref: api#credential }
      encoding: multipart
      body: >-
        return {
          name: String(params.headline),
          object_story_spec: {
            page_id: String(params.page_id),
            instagram_user_id: String(params.instagram_account_id),
            link_data: {
              message: String(params.text),
              name: String(params.headline),
              link: String(params.landing_page),
              picture: String(params.image_url),
              call_to_action: { type: params.call_to_action || 'LEARN_MORE', value: { link: String(params.landing_page) } }
            }
          }
        }
      transport: json
      okOn: [400, 403]
      error: { $ref: api#error }
    # On, inside a paused campaign: it goes to Meta's review now and serves only once the
    # campaign is switched on.
    - name: ad
      method: POST
      url: "return 'https://graph.facebook.com/v26.0/act_' + encodeURIComponent(params.account_id) + '/ads'"
      credential: { $ref: api#credential }
      encoding: multipart
      body: >-
        return {
          name: String(params.headline),
          adset_id: String(params.ad_set_id),
          creative: { creative_id: String(calls.creative.id) },
          status: 'ACTIVE'
        }
      transport: json
      okOn: [400, 403]
      error: { $ref: api#error }
  returns: >-
    return { ok: true, ad_id: String(calls.ad.id), creative_id: String(calls.creative.id) }

change_campaign:
  description: >-
    Pause or archive a campaign, or lower its daily budget. It never switches a campaign on or
    raises a budget: those spend more, and are a person's yes.
  calls:
    # What it is now, so a budget can be checked as lower.
    - name: current
      method: GET
      url: "return 'https://graph.facebook.com/v26.0/' + encodeURIComponent(params.campaign_id) + '?fields=status,daily_budget'"
      credential: { $ref: api#credential }
      transport: json
      okOn: [400, 403]
      error: { $ref: api#error }
    - name: change
      when: >-
        return (!params.status || ['PAUSED', 'ARCHIVED'].indexOf(params.status) !== -1)
          && (!params.daily_budget || Math.round(Number(params.daily_budget) * 100) <= Number((calls.current || {}).daily_budget || 0))
          && !!(params.status || params.daily_budget)
      method: POST
      url: "return 'https://graph.facebook.com/v26.0/' + encodeURIComponent(params.campaign_id)"
      credential: { $ref: api#credential }
      encoding: multipart
      body: >-
        return Object.fromEntries(Object.entries({
          status: params.status,
          daily_budget: params.daily_budget ? Math.round(Number(params.daily_budget) * 100) : undefined
        }).filter(e => e[1] !== undefined && e[1] !== null && e[1] !== ''))
      transport: json
      okOn: [400, 403]
      error: { $ref: api#error }
  # Refused rather than thrown, so an agent reads why and does not retry the same thing.
  returns: >-
    return calls.change
      ? { ok: true, campaign_id: String(params.campaign_id), status: params.status || (calls.current || {}).status, daily_budget: params.daily_budget || Number((calls.current || {}).daily_budget || 0) / 100 }
      : { ok: false, error: 'change_campaign only pauses, archives or lowers a budget; switching on or raising a budget needs a person\'s yes' }

report:
  description: >-
    Spend and results per campaign in an ad account, from a start date (YYYY-MM-DD, default 30
    days ago) to today or an end date. Optionally only some campaigns.
  calls:
    - name: insights
      method: GET
      url: >-
        return 'https://graph.facebook.com/v26.0/act_' + encodeURIComponent(params.account_id)
          + '/insights?level=campaign&limit=100'
          + '&fields=campaign_id,campaign_name,spend,impressions,reach,clicks,inline_link_clicks'
          + '&time_range=' + encodeURIComponent(JSON.stringify({
              since: params.since || Date.iso(Date.now() - 30 * 86400000).split('T')[0],
              until: params.until || Date.iso(Date.now()).split('T')[0]
            }))
          + ((params.campaign_ids || []).length
              ? '&filtering=' + encodeURIComponent(JSON.stringify([{ field: 'campaign.id', operator: 'IN', value: params.campaign_ids }]))
              : '')
      credential: { $ref: api#credential }
      transport: json
      okOn: [400, 403]
      error: { $ref: api#error }
  returns: >-
    return {
      ok: true,
      campaigns: (response.data || []).map(r => ({
        campaign_id: String(r.campaign_id),
        name: r.campaign_name,
        spend: Number(r.spend || 0),
        impressions: Number(r.impressions || 0),
        reach: Number(r.reach || 0),
        clicks: Number(r.clicks || 0),
        link_clicks: Number(r.inline_link_clicks || 0)
      }))
    }
files.interface.yaml:
inputs:
  - name: input
    type: object
    description: Trigger. When the graph runs this node it lists the ad accounts and Instagram accounts the token can reach.

outputs:
  - name: output
    type: object
    description: The ad accounts and Instagram accounts, or Meta's reason it could not list them

credentials:
  - name: metaAccessToken
    required: true
    displayName: Meta

serviceConnectors:
  - name: mcpService
    serviceType: mcp
    isService: true
    methods: [list_accounts, find_targeting, list_campaigns, create_campaign, create_ad, change_campaign, report]
    description: >-
      MCP tools for an agent: find ad accounts, the Instagram account and targeting, create
      Instagram campaigns and image ads, pause them or lower their budget, read their results.
files.node.yaml:
type: MetaAdsMCP
kind: PromiseNode
name: Instagram Ads
category: Go To Market
color: "#0866FF"
# Attached to an agent over a service edge rather than wired in sequence.
template: service
description: Run Instagram ad campaigns. Find targeting, create campaigns and image ads paused, pause them, read their results.
whenToUse: >
  Pick to advertise on Instagram: find an ad account, the Instagram account to post as and the
  targeting to use (countries, job titles, industries, interests), create a campaign and its
  image ads, pause it or lower its budget, and read spend and results per campaign. Campaigns
  are created paused and this node never switches one on, so nothing it does spends more.
  Attach it via a service edge to an agent, or trigger it directly to list the accounts.

# WHO MAY RUN THIS (DECLARATIVE_NODES.md §9.13). Compulsory on every node, so that a node
# nobody thought about cannot look the same as one deliberately left open.
#
# `required: false` adds no requirement of its own: the node runs for whoever the trigger
# admitted. The trigger instance's publicEntry toggle still owns the door, and requirements
# only ever narrow.
